title: Taste 90 Years of LA Deli History | Canter’s – Los Angeles
description:
Meet your host: Marc. Third-generation owner of Canter's Deli, he’s spent his life inside one of LA’s most iconic institutions, carrying forward a story that started long before him.

If you want to understand Los Angeles, don’t just chase what’s new. Sit at the counter. Order something that’s been on the menu for decades. Listen to the stories that only exist because someone stayed.

Canter’s isn’t just a deli. It’s late nights, neon lights, and booths that have seen everything. Musicians, actors, locals, regulars. The kind of place where history doesn’t sit on a wall, it lives in the room.

This isn’t just a meal. It’s a walk through 90 years of LA, told by someone who’s part of it. Pastrami, matzo ball soup, black and white cookies, and the stories behind it all.

Book a tasting with Marc and you’ll see the city differently. Not just where to go, but what’s lasted. The places that don’t change, even when everything around them does.

title: Where Fees Go April 2019 | Host Q&A | Airbnb
description:
Airbnb hosts asked the question: “What does Airbnb do with the hosting fees it collects?” Hosts and guests are usually charged a service fee whenever a booking or Experience is confirmed. The money that’s collected is invested into three big categories—community support, marketing, and product development—to help support hosts. In the past year, for instance, Airbnb built a new process online so that hosts can get assistance in whichever way they prefer—our online chat system or on the phone—more quickly. Next is marketing, which helps Airbnb stay top of mind for travelers when they’re looking for places to stay and things to do—and, ultimately, help bring you more guests. We focus mainly on three types of marketing: traditional advertising, online, and other campaigns via Airbnb’s website and mobile app. And finally, we’re investing in product development, and building the tools and infrastructure to power hosts’ businesses and to help them succeed.

title: Location Reviews April 2019 | Host Q&A | Airbnb
description:
Airbnb hosts asked the question: “Does Airbnb have any plans to rephrase the location category in reviews? Location reviews seem to depend on a guest’s opinion, rather than a standard of service.” Yes! In fact, we recently published a blog post recapping the improvements we’ve made to the review system. Now, when a guest rates you in the location category, if they give you three stars or fewer, they’ll see an additional question: “Was the listing’s location not described accurately?” So far, this change has led to an increase in the average rating for location. Laura Chambers, Airbnb’s general manager of Homes Host, says it’s also important to clarify that the location category rating doesn’t impact a host’s overall rating or eligibility for Superhost status. She talks more about the fix and other changes that have made reviews more fair for hosts.

title: Applying human values in your work and life with Greta Bradman | Experts Unleashed | Atlassian
description:
Greta Bradman wears many “expert” hats. Psychologist, AI scientist, founder & advisor, ABC broadcaster, former no. 1 recording artist/ freelance classical singer…the list goes on. As a coach, Greta works with leaders from business, tech, sports, entertainment, and the arts to enhance performance, leadership, and well-being. Greta is especially passionate about human values and helping people make choices that feel right in the long run, even when they’re tough in the moment. In 2025, Greta released her first book, “What Matters to You: How Values Transform Your Work and Life,” a practical field guide to understanding and applying human values in everyday decision-making.

During this episode of "Experts Unleashed," Atlassian's Dom Price chats with Greta about the power of human values, how values emerge and evolve in organizations, and the future of value-based decision making in the world of AI. Greta shares the difference between growth-based values and threat-based values (something we all have), the typical value lifecycle within an organization, and why values-alignment will be the biggest struggle for AI as we use it more. Greta’s deep understanding of human values, along with her ability to simplify such a complex topic, will have you reexamining your own values before the end of the episode!

They also discuss the "My User Manual" Play from Atlassian's Team Playbook. It's an exercise designed to help leaders share with their teams and teammates HOW they work. Think of it like this: when you buy a TV, it comes with a User Manual. But when you hire a human, there's no such helpful guidance. Greta takes us through her User Manual and shares her top three values…the headline of her values would read “serially curious!”

title: Kene Anoliefo: How to build context libraries and raise AI fluency | Product in Practice
description:
Kene Anoliefo has led product and design at Google, Spotify, and Netflix. She founded Heard, an AI-powered user research platform, and is now building tools that help teams capture and structure institutional knowledge so both people and AI can produce consistently high-quality work.

We discuss:
- The three Ps of AI adoption: people, process, and platform
- Why most companies jump to platform tools whilst ignoring the people problem
- Moving from gatekeepers to architects in product organisations
- Context enablement: turning implicit knowledge into explicit AI inputs
- The coordination tax and how AI changes team collaboration
- Why AI is like a brilliant but clueless new team member
- Building context libraries to 10x your AI output quality

Key takeaways:
Start with people, not platform tools. Most companies rush to buy AI tools whilst ignoring the deeper questions: Who am I in this AI era? What makes me valuable when AI can do parts of my job? Anxiety about AI is rooted in identity, not technology. Address the people layer first - help your team understand their evolving roles - before investing in new platforms.

Transform from gatekeepers to architects. Don't own user research, product strategy, or design - architect the principles and standards so anyone can do great work in those domains. With AI giving everyone superpowers, your value shifts from creating scarcity to enabling abundance. Make it an explicit team goal to help others do work that used to require specialists.

Context is your competitive advantage, not just data. AI trained on generic internet data produces generic output. Context libraries - structured repositories of your product strategy, design principles, customer segments, and research standards - help AI understand how your company specifically builds products. The investment in documenting this context has a multiplier effect on output quality.

AI is brilliant but clueless without your context. Think of AI as a talented new hire who needs onboarding. It has incredible capabilities but no understanding of your product, customers, or how your team works. Just like you'd explain these things to a new employee, you need to explicitly provide this context to AI tools through documentation optimised for machine reading.

Don't wait for permission to engage with AI. The biggest barrier isn't technical knowledge - it's mindset. You don't need to have worked at ML-first companies or taken AI courses. The cure for AI anxiety isn't trying to learn everything; it's starting with work you already love and asking how AI can make it 10-20% better. Focus on one thing, see results, then expand.

title: Ravi Mehta: Data-driven prototyping with AI | Product in Practice
description:
Ravi Mehta is a senior product executive with experience leading product organisations at TripAdvisor, Facebook, and Tinder. He's the co-creator of Reforge's AI Strategy Program and currently works as a full-time product strategy adviser and investor with consumer brands and fast-growing startups.

Key takeaways:
AI generates the average - and that's both its strength and limitation. Large language models are trained on existing data, which means they excel at producing "pretty good" results quickly. But exceptional products aren't average - they're outliers. The goal isn't to move faster towards average solutions, but to use AI's speed to iterate rapidly towards something truly exceptional for your users.

Product work is splitting into human-speed and AI-speed activities. Understanding customers, creating a strategy, and building adoption happen at human speed. Writing documentation, creating prototypes, and increasingly design work happen at AI speed. The most successful product managers will focus on human-speed activities - customer discovery, product sense, and strategy - because these are where you add unique value.

The emphasis is shifting from craft to taste. Creating things used to require both taste (knowing what to build) and craft (the ability to build it). AI is democratising craft across creative fields. When anyone can generate beautiful designs or working prototypes, taste becomes the primary differentiator. For product managers, determining what to build becomes 90% of success, up from roughly 50% before.

Data-driven prototyping unlocks more sophisticated testing. Rather than starting with specifications or designs, begin with the data schema that will drive your experience. Generate mock data (or pull from existing systems), then ask AI to create an interface around that data. This creates better separation between presentation and data layers, makes iteration faster, and produces more realistic prototypes for user testing.

Three cohorts exist in every organisation: evangelists, interested learners, and sceptics. Evangelists are already experimenting daily. Interested learners need access and education to get started. Sceptics need to understand that whilst AI won't fulfil all the hype, it's genuinely transformative. People who refuse to engage with AI tools will fall behind in pace - not because AI replaces them, but because they're moving slower than necessary.

title: Laura Burkhauser: Building AI habits that ship | Product in Practice
description:
Laura Burkhauser is CEO at Descript, where she's building AI-powered video editing tools that are changing how creators work. She's previously led product at Twitter, Rent the Runway, and The Tote. She's recognized for launching Underlord, Descript's AI co-editor, and expanding what's possible in creator productivity.

Key takeaways:
Don't lead with fear, lead with excitement. Rather than being driven by FOMO and the "burning platform" of AI disruption, discover your "beach moment" - something that genuinely excites you about AI's potential. For Laura, it was successfully shipping an undo button to production using Cursor and Claude. Once you experience that superpower feeling, investing in learning becomes natural.

Start with simulate, then automate, then delegate. Avoid immediately purchasing AI tools or attempting to automate everything. Begin by simulating workflows manually to validate the concept (as Laura did with post-launch tasks). Then build or purchase automation once you've proven it works. Finally, delegate when the system is dependable enough to run with minimal oversight.

Context is the new currency for career advancement. Junior employees previously earned their way into key meetings by creating slides or taking notes - tasks AI now handles. Today's juniors must identify new ways to provide value that leverage their AI-native abilities, gaining access to the context that will make them strategic leaders.

AI won't replace creativity; it amplifies it. In creative workflows, AI isn't about delegation - it's about achieving things you never thought possible. Laura went from creating 30-second clips to producing 30-minute videos. The objective isn't to hand off creative work, but to give creators superpowers to execute their vision more quickly.

Get your whole team to vibe code something. Laura required everyone on her product team to set up Cursor and prototype something they'd wanted to build but couldn't justify resources for. Once designers could handle their own VQA and PMs could ship features independently, the team was fully bought in. The experience of power drives adoption.

title: Why PMs who can't build will get left behind | Elena Verna | Product in Practice
description:
Elena Verna is Head of Growth at Lovable, one of the fastest-growing AI-native companies. She's previously held growth and product leadership roles at Dropbox, Miro, Amplitude, and SurveyMonkey, where she built some of the most influential frameworks in product-led growth.

We discuss
- The shift from "product manager" to "product builder" and why interviews now require working prototypes
- Automating Growth 101 work so you can focus on creative strategy
- The collapse of the talent stack: how roles in product, design, and engineering are blurring
- Three things that won't change: customer interaction, vision setting, and understanding distribution
- The "superpower framework" for career-accelerating decisions

Key takeaways
- PMs who can't build are becoming obsolete. The shift isn't theoretical or five years away. Top tech companies are already changing their interview processes to require functional prototypes instead of case studies. If you can't translate your product thinking into something tangible, you're competing with one hand behind your back.
- Automate Growth 101, then invest the freed-up time in creative strategy. The repetitive mechanics of growth marketing (A/B tests, funnel analysis, campaign setup) are increasingly automatable with AI. Elena argues that the PMs who thrive will be the ones redirecting that time toward the harder, more creative work that machines can't do yet.
- The talent stack is collapsing, and that's exciting. Boundaries between product, design, and engineering are blurring as AI gives individuals more autonomy across disciplines. Elena sees this as liberating rather than threatening. The PMs who embrace building, not just specifying, can move faster and validate ideas without waiting for a team to assemble.
- Three foundations won't change, no matter how good AI gets. Customer interaction, vision setting, and understanding distribution remain irreplaceably human. AI can accelerate execution, but it can't replace the judgment that comes from sitting with customers, setting a compelling direction, or knowing how your product actually reaches people.
- Your superpower lives at the intersection of what you're good at and what you love. Elena's career accelerated when she stopped trying to be well-rounded and started leaning into product-led growth as her defining skill. Find that intersection, then make career moves that compound on it rather than scattering your energy across unrelated opportunities.

title: Share artifacts between parent and child pipelines | Bitbucket Blitz | Atlassian
description:
Bitbucket Pipelines lets you build reusable pipelines and share them across repositories.

These reusable, shared pipelines need a way to share artifacts.

Otherwise, we’ll have to repeat expensive steps such as downloading and installing dependencies and building the application code.

You can now specify an artifacts section for child pipelines, with upload and download keywords.

Artifacts listed under upload will be moved from the parent pipeline into the child pipeline, where they can be used and potentially modified.

Artifacts listed under download will be moved from the child pipeline, up a level, to the calling parent pipeline, where they can be used and potentially passed to other child pipelines.

In this way, a parent pipeline could download artifacts from a build child pipeline and then upload them to a testing child pipeline.

Learn more about sharing artifacts between parent and child pipelines here: https://www.atlassian.com/blog/bitbucket/share-artifacts-between-parent-and-child-pipelines

title: How to Shave: Tips for Getting the Best Shave from Dollar Shave Club
description:
Shaving is easy if you know how —  here are some tips to get the best shave of your life: 

1. Wash your face with warm water and a good exfoliating prep scrub to remove any gunk — including dirt and dead skin cells — that would otherwise clog up your blade. Alternatively, you can use a hot towel to soften up your whiskers and open your pores, making it easier for the razor to glide smoothly across your face and effortlessly slice through the hairs.

2. Choose a shave product that’ll lubricate your skin and soften the hairs without drying out your face. The type of shave aid you use is down to personal preference: Shave cream is traditional for a pillowy, smooth shave, but those who want to be able to see where they’re shaving more clearly — if, for example, they’re experimenting with some different beard styles — may want to try a soft, transparent shave butter instead.

3. It’s vital to know how to shave with the grain (especially around the crease of the neck), as it helps to prevent razor burn, skin irritation and ingrown hair (if you try to go against the grain and discover that your skin generally isn’t prone to irritation, then shaving this way is certainly a one-way trip to Smooth City — just be aware that this isn’t true for most people.)

4. For cheeks as smooth as a baby’s bottom, make your razor strokes long and apply a consistent amount of pressure.

5. A shave isn’t over when you put the razor down — proper aftercare soothes your skin when it needs it most. Since shaving is a natural exfoliant, make sure you always apply a gentle alcohol-free post shave cream afterwards to put back what you took out by shaving. This will help to soothe, nourish and hydrate your skin.

6. Check it out! You’re even more handsome now that you can actually see your own face! And all it took was a few basics: The right preparation, knowing how to shave with the grain, and how to care for your skin afterwards. We told you it’s easy when you know how.

Check out more helpful videos in the Dollar Shave Club How To Library of How To’s here on YouTube, or head to DollarShaveClub.com.

title: CEO Drew Houston on solving the biggest problem with modern work
description:
For our seventh episode of Working Smarter (https://workingsmarter.ai/)  we’re talking to Drew Houston, the co-founder and CEO of Dropbox. 


If you’ve been online long enough, it’s likely Dropbox was your introduction to the cloud. The goal is still more or less the same—give you one organized place for all your stuff—but it’s no longer just about storing and syncing files. A hundred files on your desktop is now a hundred tabs in your browser, and Houston believes AI is what will finally bring calm to the chaos that’s been created by the tools of modern work.


For Houston, AI’s potential is so great that its arrival feels like a civilization shift. It’s also not just a professional preoccupation; AI is a personal interest too. A few years ago he decided to teach himself machine learning in his spare time—and some of the AI tools Houston now uses to run Dropbox are ones he built himself. 


Hear Houston discuss why it’s gotten so hard to find the information you need to do your job, the types of tasks we'll increasingly offload to our silicon brains, and what Dropbox is doing to help make modern work more meaningful and fulfilling.

title: Sophia Wang on the new tools helping her find answers in old data
description:
On our final episode this season of Working Smarter (https://workingsmarter.ai/)  we talk to Sophia Wang, an assistant professor of ophthalmology at Stanford University. 


Wang leads the school’s ophthalmic informatics and artificial intelligence group, which uses the latest machine learning techniques to analyze electronic health records. In practice, that means looking at disparate sources of data—from doctors’ notes and eye exam data to diagnostic imagery and billing codes—and finding the sorts of patterns that can be difficult for humans to spot.


Hear Wang talk about using AI to extract useful information from a sea of unstructured data, and how to make better decisions with the data you already have—which, in Wang’s case, means improving outcomes for glaucoma patients and providing a better quality of care.

Very few people get paid to visit shipwrecks—but for Stephanie Gandulla, it’s all part of the job. She’s an assistant professor at the University of Michigan and the director of the school’s Field Robotics Group. title: Benedikt Lehnert on AI’s Real Adoption Curve: Design Is the Diffuser
description:
Design doesn’t just make tech usable—it makes it adoptable. Benedikt Lehnert is a design executive and Entrepreneurship and Design Fellow, at Princeton University. In this interview he draws on history to walk through his take on AI as Normal Technology and how design will accelerate (or hinder) AI’s diffusion.

We trace the path from steam and electrification to the personal computer and today’s AI systems—showing how design translates human intent into action. And, we discuss lessons from the PC productization, a Bauhaus for AI idea, and what skills (taste, craft, critical thinking) matter most in the age of generative models.

What you’ll learn
- Ben’s thoughts on AI’s diffusion timeline
- How design bridges invention → adoption → diffusion
- The role of productization (e.g., Macintosh) in making tech personal
- Why a “Bauhaus for AI” blends data literacy, ethics, and craft
- Practical skills to differentiate beyond average, AI-generated outputs

title: FigBrew: Understanding The Next Era Of Strategy With Tamara Moellenberg
description:
What if looking at the world the way designers do could unlock a company’s next competitive edge?

In this episode of FigBrew, Andrew Hogan speaks with Tamara Moellenberg, associate partner at ReD Associates, about a strategy framework that goes beyond optimization and user-centricity. Drawing on anthropology, ethnography, and the social sciences, Moellenberg introduces the idea of “worlds” as a third wave of strategy, focused on culture, communities, and shared systems of meaning.

Together, they explore why many classic strategy tools no longer explain outsized success, how companies like Hermès and LEGO build value by tapping into cultural worlds, and why understanding energy, relevance, and social dynamics can matter more than market size alone. The conversation also touches on how generative AI raises the stakes for cultural resonance and what it means for organizations navigating uncertainty.

You’ll learn:
• Why traditional strategy frameworks are no longer enough
• How “worlds” explain cultural advantage and differentiation
• What companies like Hermès and LEGO get right
• How to think about energy, relevance, and the right to win
• Why generative AI makes cultural resonance more important

title: Why Design, Strategy, and Technology Are Inseparable
description:
Design strategy spans business intent and execution, but it’s rarely taught or practiced that way.

In this episode of FigBrew, Andrew Hogan sits down with Garkay Wong, author of The Art of Design Strategy, to explore how designers can better articulate the value of their work in an era of rapid technological change. Drawing on her experience across service design, innovation strategy, and consulting, Wong explains why many traditional business frameworks fall short and how design can play a stronger role in strategic decision-making.

The conversation centers on TRACES, Wong’s framework for aligning design work with organizational goals by accounting for technical debt, regulation, audience shifts, competition, economic forces, and substitute technologies. Together, they discuss why alignment matters more than brainstorming, how collaboration between designers and non-designers is evolving, and what it means to make ideas tangible in order to improve decision quality.

They also examine how generative AI is increasing teams’ capacity to create, why prioritization matters more than ever, and why judgment, context, and craft remain essential as production accelerates.

What you’ll learn
• Why designers often struggle to communicate value to the business
• How the TRACES framework helps teams align and make better decisions
• Why technology now sits at the center of strategy conversations
• How collaboration between designers and non-designers is changing
• What generative AI means for capacity, prioritization, and craft

Together, they unpack the rebound in design hiring, the surge in demand for senior ICs, and the state of junior hiring. Daniel shares what he’s seeing firsthand from running design leadership searches across industries — and where companies may be thinking too short-term.

From the quest for a “founding designer unicorn” to the Moneyball approach to building teams, this conversation reframes how design talent should be evaluated, developed, and structured for the current environment.

They also explore what AI literacy really signals to employers, why mentorship and player development matter more than ever, and what candidates should be doing differently right now.

You’ll learn:
 • What our new hiring study reveals about the design market
 • Differences between hiring in 2024, 2025, and today's environment
 • What “leadership” in design really means (beyond titles)
 • Why the founding designer role is often misunderstood
 • The danger of hiring only senior ICs
 • Why most startups should think like Moneyball, not the Yankees
 • How flattening orgs hurt mentorship and long-term development
 • Why experience diversity matters as much as other forms of diversity
 • What candidates should actually be doing to stand out
 • How to build AI case studies if your company hasn’t adopted AI yet

description:
Learn how Slots unlock dynamic components instances — from adding another menu option, button, or even an icon to your instances, without detaching.

Slots are great for:

• Components with repeating elements, like task lists or tabs.
• Components that are frequently customized, like cards or modals.
• Simplifying bloated design systems by decreasing variants or hidden layers.
• Reducing detaches so instances continue receiving updates from the main component.

Rolling out now in open beta over the next week. Available to everyone on a full-seat.

title: NoiseFit Voyage | How to's & unboxing
description:
Here's India's 1st homegrown e-sim 4G calling smartwatch, NoiseFit Voyage.
It comes with a 1.4" Retina Amoled display, inbuilt GPS and Glonass for perfect navigation on our app.

Few of the class apart features :

1. E-sim supported 4G calling
2. Can connect any TWS with the smartwatch
3. Comes with a heart rate sensor, SPO2 sensor, pedometer,etc.
4. Automatic sensors for automatic detection of heart rate, SPO2, sleep data with analytics.
5. Upto 30 days of battery life on power saving mode.
6. IP68 water rating

How to setup and use e-sim with NoiseFit Voyage smartwatch.

Few important points to remember before setting up the e-sim.

1. Separate number is required to configure on to the e-sim.
2. Smartphones with e-sim support are required to configure the e-sim on the NoiseFit Voyage.

The setup :

1. Go to Playstore or app store and download NoiseFit Voyage app.
2. Download the app and pair the watch with the app.
3. Go to my device on the app and click on Manage eSim.
4. Select your network operator - Reliance Jio or Airtel.

For Airtel eSim users :

A. Using the Airtel thanks app

1. Download the Airtel thanks app.
2. Insert the new or existing sim in the phone that has eSim support.
3. Copy the EID number from the NoiseFit Voyage app.
4. Open the airtel thanks app - upgrade to eSim - Get eSim for another device - paste the EID number - Click on Get OTP - Continue.
5. Go back to the NoiseFit Voyage app and click on the Activate button available under the EID number and wait for the eSim to be downloaded on the watch.

It may take a minute for the whole setup.

B. Visiting the official Airtel store

1. Visit the store and ask for a new eSim number.
2. Visit the NoiseFit Voyage app and repeat the same process in the steps above and select Airtel and select the second option - Open at your nearby telecom partner store.
3. Now show the EID number bar code to the Airtel executive and they will scan the code and activate the number.
4. Come back on the NoiseFit Voyage app and click on the Activate button available on the NoiseFit Voyage app.

Wait for sometime and your eSim will get downloaded and activated on the NoiseFit Voyage smartwatch.

C. If you already have an eSim or QR code

1. Insert the new/existing sim in a smartphone having eSim support.
2. Visit the Airtel website and follow the procedure available on their website to receive a barcode on your registered e-mail id.
3. Repeat the same process on your NoiseFit Voyage app and select Airtel and then choose the third option of - Already have an eSim or QR code.
4. Click on the Scan QR code button and scan the Bar code you received on your registered e-mail id.

Wait for sometime and the eSim will be downloaded on the NoiseFit Voyage smartwatch.

For Jio eSim users :

A. By scanning EID/IMEI barcode information

1. You've to visit the nearest Jio store.
2. Ask for the new eSim and complete the KYC process.
3. After completing the KYC process, go to NoiseFit Voyage app and click Manage eSim on the app and go to Jio and select the first option.
4. Show the EID number bar code to the Jio executive at the store, they will scan the barcode.
5. The eSim will get Activated and will get downloaded on your NoiseFit Voyage app.

Note : It might take some minutes for the eSim to get downloaded on the Noisefit Voyage smartwatch.

title: GoPro LIVE: Freeride World Tour 2025 | Val Thorens Pro
description:
The '25 FWT is back underway for the second stop of the season at France's Val Thorens. The world’s best snow athletes will take on the breathtaking Lac Noir face for the very first time in Freeride World Tour competition. Constant snowfalls over the past week have blanketed the mountain in deep powder, setting the stage for an explosion of turns, incredible jumps, and soft landings that will undoubtedly elevate the riders' performances.
About the Venue:
Known for its technical and playful terrain, Lac Noir is set to challenge the world’s top skiers + snowboarders in an event that promises thrilling performances. Standing tall with a summit altitude of 8,200ft (2,500m) + a finish line at 6,594ft (2,010m), it is one of the season's most exciting + technical venues. This dreamy face is a haven for the stacked ski + snowboard field, boasting an average steepness of 37°, + a maximum pitch of 43°.
The venue begins from a wide ridge, offering a playground of possibilities. With its natural terrain movements, big rock features, + a ridge with countless line options, Lac Noir is a canvas for creativity. Divided into three distinct stages, the venue provides a mix of challenges + opportunities that will test the riders' skills + orientation. Rollovers and terrain transitions create moments of difficulty, requiring precise navigation + control. Starting with an immediate jump off the ridge, competitors will have to bring their A-game from the very first moment.

title: GoPro LIVE: Freeride World Tour 2025 | Xtreme Verbier
description:
The stage is set for the FWT grand finale at the YETI Xtreme Verbier by Honda—the ultimate freeride showdown. World titles are on the line at the 30th anniversary of the legendary event on Switzerland's Bec des Rosses. The competition will feature three starts instead of the traditional summit start; two on the Petit Bec offering highly technical, steep lines with exposed terrain and one start half way down the central couloir leading into the heart of the Bec, where riders must navigate chutes and natural airs. With reverse ranking order in each category, the highest-ranked riders will drop last, building tension until the final runs. Marcus Goguen, Justine Dufour-Lapointe, Victor De Le Rue and Noémi Equy are currently leading their categories. Watch as the top ski and snowboard athletes put their skills to the test to determine who will claim the 2025 FWT title.
About the Venue:
The iconic Bec des Rosses in Verbier rises to 3,223 meters with a 600-meter vertical drop. Known for its extreme 50-degree sectors, this face offers a complex web of steep couloirs, cliff drops, and highly technical lines. It demands both skill and bravery, as riders must navigate a multitude of challenges while maintaining control and style. The Bec des Rosses is regarded as the ultimate proving ground for freeriders, where the world’s best come to cement their legacies.

title: Perfect Sunrise at Cappadocia Balloon Festival
description:
Experience Cappadocia, Turkey like never before—through the eyes of FPV pilot Jackson Goldblatt's lens as he flew his drone through one of the world’s most surreal landscapes home to the iconic Cappadocia Hot Air Balloon Festival. Shot entirely on GoPro, this cinematic 4K flight takes you soaring between ancient rock formations, sweeping past dozens of colorful hot air balloons, and diving through the valleys that have made this region a travel bucket list destination.

Nestled in central Turkey, Cappadocia has been shaped for millions of years by volcanic activity and erosion — it was shaped by two giant volcanoes, Erciyes and Hasan. An old Anatolian tale reads that two volcano gods were rivals that fought by spewing fire and ash and their battles sculpted Cappadocia’s valleys. Modern balloonists like to say the balloons’ flames “wake up” the ancient fire spirits every morning.

Watch as Jackson's launches into sunrise capturing sweeping shots across Göreme National Park, every moment designed to immerse you in the feeling of being right there in the sky.

title: GoPro Awards: Saving a Life
description:
Carson Schmidt and Erik Masuda didn’t hesitate when they spotted a terrifying scene on the mountain: a skier trapped upside down in deep snow, one of the most dangerous situations in winter sports.

In heavy powder conditions, snow submersion accidents can happen fast. Skiers and snowboarders can become disoriented, buried, and unable to breathe within seconds if their airway is blocked.

Watch as Carson and Erik act quickly, stay calm under pressure, and heroically perform a life-saving rescue by digging toward the victim’s face to clear their airway.

Ski & Snowboard Safety Reminder:
- Always ride with a partner on deep powder days
- Keep each other in sight at all times
- Be aware of tree wells and deep snow hazards
- Act FAST in an emergency—every second counts

If you ever face a situation like this, stay calm, assess quickly, and prioritize clearing the airway immediately. For more information on winter safety, head to https://safety.skicalifornia.org

title: Skills, Talents and Aspirations
description:
When people are forced to leave their homes, they have to leave most things behind. But no matter what they leave behind, they all bring three things with them wherever they go: skills, talents, aspirations.

The IKEA Foundation is supporting the International Rescue Committee (IRC) with a €5 million grant to help improve the lives of both refugees and young Kenyans living in Nairobi’s informal settlements. Together we promote refugees’ self-reliance and financial independence. 
 
Refugees and their new communities can thrive together when refugees are able to develop their skills, embrace their talents and fulfil their aspirations. Because when refugees are able to work, they create businesses and employ others. They have more money to spend in the local economy and need fewer benefits. They experience less frustration and feel more connected to their new community, like Patience, Lispher and Sebineza are.

title: IDAHOT 2020: Be Someone’s Home
description:
On IDAHOT 17 May, the International Day Against Homophobia, Transphobia & Biphobia, we’re calling on our customers and co-workers to make LGBT+ people feel at home everywhere, every day.

For many of us, a forced quarantine during 2020 has taught us how important our home is. A place where we can feel safe, where we can love and feel loved. But there are some who risk being stigmatised, isolated and discriminated against in their living spaces. For the LGBT+ community, their four walls are not always what make them feel at home and welcomed.

With the Be Someone’s Home campaign 2020, we want to recognise this reality and invite co-workers and customers to be a shelter for those who are discriminated against and struggle to find safety. We can be a safe space for our LGBT+ friends and colleagues, we can be their home.

Everyone should have the right to be themselves. Stand up against discrimination of LGBT+ persons on 17 May, and every day #BeSomeonesHome #IDAHOT

title: IKEA Sustainability Report FY23 Highlights
description:
2023 was another challenging year for people and businesses around the world. In difficult times such as these, we believe it’s more important than ever not to lose focus on our sustainability ambitions. We need to work even harder to keep moving in the right direction.

This year, we decreased our climate footprint by 22% in absolute terms compared to baseline FY16. We’ve also updated our climate goals and accelerated our climate actions in line with the 1.5°C trajectory and the SBTi Net-Zero Standard. 

We’ve taken many other actions during the year, including, for the first time, using bio-based glue at an IKEA Industry board factory. As glue represents approximately 5% of the total IKEA climate footprint, moving from fossil-based to bio-based glue is key to reaching our overall climate goal. We’ve also pioneered a new technology that enables fibreboard recyclability.

We’ve reduced the amount of plastic packaging in consumer goods by approximately 47% and decreased the total plastic packaging (including consumer packs, multipacks, unit loads and handling materials) by approximately 44% compared with FY21.

We’ve continued our work contributing to a fair and equal society, including launching our updated People Strategy to strengthen our direction and ambition for equality, diversity, and inclusion.

You can read about our progress in the IKEA Sustainability and Climate Reports FY23.

title: Rediscover Andaman with Shenaz Treasury
description:
I believe that even if I manage to travel the entire world someday, my heart will forever stay biased towards #MyIndia🇮🇳 ❤️. India is a complete package of beauty, culture, heritage, and the new-age world. How can one not fall in love, tell me?
One of my most favourite places in India is Andaman Island. Surrounded by surreal beaches, sand, and crystal clear water, this place is no less than a paradise🌊 🏖️ 🐚. Apart from the famous Ross Islands and Cellular Jail, there’s so much more to explore here. These are the hidden gems I found during my trip💎 📍: 
 
✨ Natural Bridges, Neil Island: A masterpiece of nature, I must say. This place has a naturally shaped bridge-like rock, which is also known as the Howrah Bridge. 🗿 🌉
 
✨ Radhanagar beach: This is one of the most beautiful beaches in Asia. Its perfectly turquoise coloured water, white sand, serenity, and peaceful ambiance will instantly make you fall in love with the place. 🏖️
 
✨ Neil’s Cove: If you’re a fan of swimming and snorkeling, Neil’s Cove is THE place for you. Clear blue water and calm sea, a dream for all! 🏊‍♀️
 
✨ Mangroves-Havelock Island: Want to take the incredible experience of Kayaking? Make sure you visit this beautiful place! 🚣‍♀️
 
✨ Sitapur beach, Neil Island: Situated at the tip of the island, this is called the ‘sunrise beach.’ If you want to experience the most magical sunrise, then don’t forget to check this beach out. 🏖️ 🌅
 
✨ Turtle beach, Havelock Island: This is a hub for all scuba diving and snorkeling enthusiasts. Visit this place and experience the surreal underwater world. 🐢

✨ Araku Valley: Filled with greenery and fresh air, this place gives a refreshing break from the hectic city life. With its exquisite biodiversity and a wide variety of coffee plantations, Araku Valley is on its way to becoming a famous tourist destination. 🤩

✨ Bojjannakonda: Rich in culture and history, Bojjannakonda is a significant tourist site in Andhra. These caves are a notable establishment of Buddhism and feature its three phases - Mahayana, Hinayana and Vajrayana.🧘🏼‍♂️

✨Mangamaripeta Beach: It is believed that this region was under the kingdom of Kalinga and later served as a promotional center for Buddhism. It also offers a wide variety of adventure sports like snorkelling, jet-skiing and scuba diving. 🤿

title: Rediscover Sikkim with Aakriti Rana
description:
With fresh air, blue skies, snow-capped mountains, and lush green valleys, Sikkim has it all in abundance⭐. I’m amazed to see that each lane and corner of this place has something unique to offer. Here are some of the hidden gems I visited📍: 

✨Snow-tsongmo lake: Covered in snow, this famous glacial lake changes colors. Truly magical, I must say. 🗻

✨Temi Tea estate: This place is a heaven for tea and nature lovers! From clear blue skies to high-quality tea production, you can find it all here. 🌱

✨Tathagata Tsal (Buddha Park): Rich in culture and history, Tathagata Tsal (Buddha Park) has a  130-foot (40 m) high statue of the Buddha as its centrepiece and is one of the most famous tourist attractions in Sikkim. 🧘🏼‍♂️

✨Ban Jhakri Falls: Majestic waterfalls and the greenery that surrounds it definitely is a treat to the eyes. One of the most beautiful getaways in Sikkim. 

✨Do Drul Chorten Monastery: Visit this Buddhist stupa in Gangtok and get a glimpse of the Buddhist culture and architecture. ⛩️

title: Rediscover Leh-Ladakh with Kritika Khurana
description:
Thanks to my job, I’ve had the opportunity to visit so many places around the country💛. But even after travelling to multiple places, I still can’t get enough of #MyIndia🇮🇳✨. The love and warmth you get here can’t be compared to any other place in the world💌🌎. Here, every city here has its essence, but one of my personal favourites is Leh-Ladakh❄️⛩️. 

The culture, calmness, and delicious authentic cuisines, make this place SO special✨. From the classic food Thumpka🍲and Momos🥟 to the Zanskar Valley and Pangong Tso Lake🙌🏼, this majestic place is nothing less than a dream for travel enthusiasts🧳☁️. Apart from these already famous places and cuisines, there’s still a lot to explore. So, here’s what I explored📍! 

✨Stok Palace: Built in 1820 by the Ladakhi men⛏️, the Stok Palace is home to the Namgyal Dynasty. The doors of this palace were opened to the common public after receiving the blessings of His Holiness Dalai Lama in 1980🏮.
✨Sangam Valley: It’s a 48 km drive from Leh, and acts as a confluence for the rivers Indus and Zanskar. 
✨Magnetic Hill: Known as the ‘Cyclops Hill’, the Magnetic Hill is located in Leh-Ladakh. The most amazing part? On these hills, things don’t seem to obey the laws of gravity, and instead of rolling downhill, they go uphill😲
✨Likir Monastery: Also known as Likir Gompa, it’s a Buddhist monastery located in Ladakh, some 52 km from Leh. Buddhists believe that the Snake King, Joker slept here at this monastery once and that the monastery is guarded by the spirits of two great snakes, namely Nanda and Taksako 👑🐍. 

If you also want to explore #MyIndia with a new perspective, Leh-Ladakh is the best place to start your ‘exploring the hidden gems’ journey 🛄💎. description:
Yes, it’s true. This is the Umngot River in Meghalaya.
This river is renowned for its exceptionally clear waters, often described as transparent or crystal clear. This clarity allows visitors to see straight to the riverbed, creating stunning visual effects and making it a popular destination for photography and sightseeing.
One of the most popular activities on the Umngot River is boating. You can take a traditional wooden boat ride or rent a paddle boat and explore the river at your own pace.
🗓️The best time to visit is during the dry season, from November to April.

title: AI & the Future of Work | Govindraj MK, CHRO | Beyond The Fabric Podcast Ep. 1
description:
Welcome to the debut episode of Beyond The Fabric, the official Myntra podcast where we speak with leaders across our business. To kick things off, we are diving into the people side of our strategy.

Is AI just a buzzword, or a total shift in how we work and grow? Myntra CHRO Govindraj MK sits down with Aparajita Sengupta (Senior Director - Creative and Curation) to discuss how to build AI literacy and maintain psychological safety in an increasingly "BANI" (Brittle, Anxious, Nonlinear, Incomprehensible) world. Discover the three unique human capabilities that technology simply cannot replace, and why doubling down on human skills matters more than ever.

title: Future of E-commerce & Strategic Partnerships | Venu Nair | Beyond The Fabric Myntra Podcast Ep. 2
description:
Welcome back to Beyond the Fabric, the official Myntra podcast where we speak with leaders across our business. In Episode 2, we decode the future of e-commerce, strategic partnerships, and the ultimate differentiator in India: Speed.

Venu Nair (Chief of Strategic Partnerships and Omnichannel at Myntra) sits down with Hema Pachisia (Senior Director, Human Capital) to discuss how global brands succeed in the Indian market and how to create a truly seamless shopping experience. Discover the evolving expectations of digital consumers, how Myntra uses data to drive personalization, and why unified retail, powered by 90-minute deliveries via M-NOW, is the future of fashion.

00:00 – Introduction
01:29 – What do strategic partnerships mean?
04:23 – How to decide which category or brand to pursue next
05:27 – What brands get wrong about online consumers
06:26 – Phygital/Omnichannel: The future of retail
07:42 – Three things Myntra offers its brand partners
09:26 – Behavioral shifts: Online vs. offline shopping experiences
10:43 – The power of data in a digital-first retail world
11:54 – One learning habit Venu heavily relies on
13:11 – The implications of quick commerce on fashion
13:56 – What is the future of retail in India?

description:
Blissclub is redefining activewear for Indian women signed not just to look good, but to move with real life. Founded in 2020 by Minu Margeret, the brand spotted a gap in the market: stylish activewear that truly supports comfort, flexibility, and confidence in everyday movement.

Through its strong partnership with #Myntra, Blissclub has been able to scale its reach, amplify its purpose and connect with women across India like never before. Myntra’s platform and consumer-first approach have been pivotal in bringing Blissclub’s community-driven vision to life, making activewear that’s inclusive, accessible and built for real movement available to millions.

description:
On this episode of Destroy: Never…

Did you know Hall of Famer Ken Griffey Jr. ran for president in 1996? Ok, not technically, but his bi-partisan style of play that united both baseball fans and non-baseball fans alike inspired Nike to create a faux presidential campaign for him during the 1996 election year. His swing? The sweetest thing ever. His swag? Influential. His character? Patriotic. We’re unboxing the bumper stickers, pins, cards, and more to remember this historical event for the first time in decades. To quote his potential 2024 running mate and Air Force 1 connoisseur Robbie Digital, “It’s not what the swoosh can do for you, but what you can do for the swoosh.”

title: Automate weekly market intelligence briefs w/ Custom Agents (full walkthrough) | Notion AI tutorial
description:
Learn how to automate a weekly market intelligence brief with *Notion Custom Agents* so your team stays ahead of competitor launches, pricing shifts, and key category news.

In this walkthrough, we build an agent that scans curated sources, compiles a structured brief with links to every source, and posts a short recap to Slack. We also add guardrails (recent-only scope, caps per competitor, and “flag gaps instead of guessing”) and test the scheduled run.

We’ll cover:

- Setting up competitor/source URLs to monitor
- Configuring Notion + Slack access and weekly scheduling
- Adding guardrails for relevance and accuracy (linked claims only)
- Formatting the brief (highlights, risks, opportunities, positioning, recommended actions)
- Testing runs + troubleshooting in the activity log

title: What do people get wrong about Oatly?
description: We know you didn’t come here to see a multinational oat company get all emo about consumer misperceptions, but it just feels like people don’t understand us a lot of the time. description: Back in the day, we didn’t have much money for advertising, so we came up with a couple ideas to spread the word about our products. title: Audition 16: Yes, chef | #Shorts | Oatly
description:
Spinach & Basil Omelette
 
Ingredients (1 omelette):
4 eggs
50 g spinach
5 g basil
A knob of plant-based butter
A dash of olive oil
Oatly Creamy Oat Spread
1/2 shallot
2–3 leaves of kale
Zest of half a lemon
Salt & pepper

Bring water to boil in a medium pot. Add spinach and basil to blanch quickly. Fill a medium bowl with cold water and ice and put a strainer in it. Move the spinach and basil from the boiling water to an ice-bath bowl. Leave to cool.

Once cool, grab spinach and basil and squeeze firmly to remove all excess water. Put the ball of spinach and basil in a blender together with the 4 eggs. Mix until smooth and strain into a clean and empty bowl.

Prepare your kale by removing the stem and cut the leaves into smaller pieces. Heat a small pan with olive oil and cook the kale with salt for a few minutes. Set aside. (Optional: burn the kale with a flame torch to give it some extra flavour and colour.) Finely chop your shallot and set aside. 

Heat the small pan with plant-based butter. Add the spinach/basil/egg mixture, add a pinch of salt and pepper, and cook the omelette slowly. Once the omelette starts to set, add a dash of Oatly Creamy Oat Spread in the middle and fold the omelette with a spatula. Serve on a plate with the kale, and top it off with lemon zest and shallots.

description:
Butternut Squash & Sage Risotto

Ingredients (serves 4):
1 big-ish butternut squash
1 tsp honey
A couple of decent glugs of olive oil
A couple of handfuls of fresh sage
1 spoonful dried rosemary
1 spoonsful dried thyme
1 large shallot
Plant-based butter
300 g Arborio rice
1 bottle of (nice) nonalcoholic white wine (chilled)
1/2 g saffron
Vegetable stock
Big dollop of Oatly Creamy Oat Fraiche
Plant-Based Parmesan
150 g cashew nuts
1 pinch garlic powder
1 pinch mustard powder
4 tbsp nutritional yeast

Prep the squash, peeling it and cutting it into 3 cm chunks. Then coat with olive oil and honey, followed by chopped sage, rosemary, and thyme. Roast the squash in the oven at 200°C for about half an hour.

While that’s roasting, chop the shallot and fry it gently in the pan with the butter. After about 5 minutes, add risotto rice and keep stirring over the heat until the rice has turned glossy.

Pour in the wine and boil until it has reduced completely. Turn down the heat and gradually add the stock a little bit at a time until the rice is cooked and the stock has been absorbed.

While the risotto is cooking, chuck the cashews, garlic powder, mustard powder, yeast, and a pinch of salt in a blender. Blitz to a fine powder—this will be the “parmesan.” Fry the sage leaves in oil until nice and crispy.

By now, the squash should be about ready. Take it out of the oven and mash most of it up, saving a few chunks. Stir the mashed squash into the risotto along with a spoonful of the Oatly Creamy Oat Fraiche and a little bit of butter.

Plate the risotto and scatter the remaining chunks of roasted squash and crispy sage, plus a good sprinkling of the homemade parmesan.

title: Lussekatten (The Saffron Bun!) | Toni TV | Oatly
description:
It’s almost Christmas time in Sweden and that means one thing — the traditional baking of Swedish saffron buns, which for the most part is straightforward unless the baking is being done by CEO Toni Petersson and his mom Ayako. 

Producer’s note: Toni TV was recorded in and around the organic oat fields of southern Sweden where Oatly has it’s offices. In order to ensure that viewers get to meet the real Toni Petersson, much of the footage was filmed without Toni’s knowledge that we were actually filming. Also, we didn’t let Toni view any of the material until just before it was released. Did we do this to trick Toni? Not entirely. We just felt that it was important for the viewer to get an honest idea of who the real Toni is and how Oatly — behind his new, off beat, dynamic and visionary leadership — is becoming a lifestyle brand that makes nutritional products to help people find ways to upgrade their lives and the health of the planet too.

title: From Feed To Food | Oatly
description:
When making a documentary you should go all in, right? Black and white. Slow. Strange but visually cool camera angles. Touching piano music. A farmer talking about important things, like how to make farming both more sustainable and profitable, in a language that only a tiny part of the world’s population understands so you can use subtitles, since making people read during a movie lets them know they are learning. Nice touch. Yeah, our short documentary “From feed to food” definitely ends up with high scores on the test: ”How documentary is your documentary?” Although the end might contain a little too much success and hope for a documentary, but that’s just something you’ll have to live with.

Read more about the research done by UNISECO, a European research project: https://uniseco-project.eu/case-study/sweden

title: Where’s The Milk? | Stop AM 171 | Oatly
description: Soon — whatever that means in the political sphere — the EU will decide on amendment 171. And in case you haven’t heard, 171 is a proposed law for plant-based censorship, that could prohibit all use of dairy-related language, packaging and imagery for plant-based foods. It might even make it illegal to share scientific facts showing that a plant-based product has a lower climate footprint than its dairy alternative. Why? Well, the milk lobby seems to think that when plant-based products use descriptions like ”alternative to yogurt” or ”not milk” or ”creamy texture”, it’s hard for consumers to tell the difference between them and dairy. Eh, is it? We decided to find out if the people of Europe really are that stupid. Enjoy the film. And sign the petition at https://www.oatly.com/stopam171.

title: U.S.S. Boatly | Yes, a boat made of Oatly
description:
This is a story about a boat, but it’s also a story about goodbyes. In the summer of 2022, a Colorado man named Nate had a vision: A boat made out of Oatly cartons. Most people wouldn’t act on such an insane vision, but Nate and his two children are not “most people”. And so, one of the greatest engineering feats of the last half century began.

Once complete, Nate and his brave (and also somewhat skeptical) children raced this beautifully branded canoe-like object down the Uncompahgre River in the 2022 Ridgway RiverFest. They won.  

That was in June. By the time we visited them in October, the great U.S.S. Boatly—it’s a brilliant play on words—was rotting outside Nate’s Colorado coffee shop. The sweet, pungent smell of fermenting river water and oat drink is an acquired taste—one apparently not acquired by the townspeople of Ridgway. And so, it was time to say goodbye to the engineering marvel that once proudly floated down a marvelous river very few people have ever heard of. 

Join us in saying goodbye to the U.S.S. Boatly.

title: Audition 48: When in doubt, call your mom | #Shorts | Oatly
description:
Steamed Pak Choi & Jamaican Festival

Ingredients (serves 4):
5 cloves of garlic
Half a red onion
5 lbs pak choi
8–10 cherry tomatoes
1/4 lb salted pollock
2 tbsp olive oil
250 ml Oatly Creamy Oat
1 sweet potato
1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
1/2 cup fine cornmeal
6 tbsp granulated sugar
2 tsp baking powder
1/2 tsp salt
3/4 cup Oatly Oat Drink Whole
Natural oil for deep frying

Prepare your vegetables by smashing the garlic, cutting the red onion into big chunks, and chopping the pak choi. Slice the cherry tomatoes. Cut the pollock into bite-sized pieces.

In a wide saucepan over a medium-low heat, add the olive oil and garlic and stir for one minute. Add the red onion and cherry tomatoes and cook for an additional 3 minutes. Next, add the Oatly Creamy Oat and salted pieces of pollock. Stir and cook for another 2 to 3 minutes. Fold in the chopped pak choi (it might seem like a lot, but after a few minutes it will wilt and easily fit in the saucepan). Add a few pinches of salt (not too much since the fish is salted). Let cook at medium-low heat for about 25 minutes.

While that’s cooking, peel and chop the sweet potato. In a small pot, bring water to a boil and add sweet potatoes. Boil until soft.

To make the festival: In a large bowl, combine the flour, cornmeal, granulated sugar, baking powder, and salt. Stir to combine and add the Oat Drink. Stir until the dough comes together. Then use your hands to lightly form the mixture into a ball. Pinch off pieces of dough and roll them into long oval shapes. The dough should make about 12 oval-shaped dumplings.

Heat a heavy bottom pot with at least 3 inches of frying oil (or use a deep fryer if you have one). Bring the heat to 350 degrees Fahrenheit (177 degrees Celsius). Once the oil has reached the correct temperature, add the dough dumplings. Fry them on all sides until golden brown. This takes about 4 to 6 minutes.

Take out the deep-fried dough dumplings with a slotted metal spoon and leave to drain off excess grease. Serve together with the pak choi and sweet potato and enjoy.

description:
Audition #10: The most important meal of the day 

Maritozzi buns 
Ingredients: 
500 g 0 flour  
90 g white sugar 
5 g instant dry yeast 
250 ml + 3 tbsp of Oatly Oat Drink Regular 
90 ml neutral oil (plus extra for brushing on dough) 
Zest of 1 orange 
Zest of 1 lemon 
1 tbsp maple syrup 
Pinch of salt 
2 tsp vanilla extract 
140 g white sugar (for syrup), plus extra for sprinkling on top 
400 ml Oatly Whippable Creamy Oat 
Powdered sugar for dusting  

Dissolve the yeast in 250 ml of Oatly Oat Drink at room temperature. Mix the flour and 90 g white sugar in a bowl and add the oil and Oat Drink mixture. Add the orange and lemon zest, maple syrup, vanilla, and salt and mix well to a soft consistency.  

Knead the dough for about 10 minutes without adding any more flour. If necessary, wet your hands with a little oil. Then place the dough in a bowl, brush it with oil, cover with plastic wrap, and let it rise in the oven (turned off) until doubled in volume (3 to 4 hours). 
 
Divide the dough into eight equal pieces (80 g each), form into balls, and stretch them gently. Let them rise again for about an hour, well covered, and then brush them lightly with the 3 tbsp of Oatly Oat Drink and bake at 180°C (350°F) for about 15 minutes.  


To make the maritozzi shiny, prepare a syrup by dissolving 140 g of sugar with 100 ml of water in a saucepan. Once the maritozzi are baked and still hot, brush them with syrup and sprinkle with a bit of sugar. 

 
Whip the Oatly Whippable Creamy Oat while the buns are cooling down. Once the buns have cooled, split them down the center without dividing them in half, open them a little, and stuff with the whipped Oatly using a scoop. The whipped Oatly should be leveled well so that it does not come out excessively. Dust them with powdered sugar and enjoy with a cup of coffee.

description:
The Ekta houseboat makes you wake up to the sight of jumping fishes and chirping birds all around while you bask in the sunlight entering from the window

Floating in Ekta Nagar, Vadodara, this facility is surrounded by over 20 tourist attractions like statue of unity, jungle safari, narmada aarti, dino trail and the boat cruise.

Even on board, there’s something for everyone! The houseboat boasts of a large and expansive observation deck on the top floor showcases the natural beauty of the narmada river. There is a drawing room in the houseboat with Bluetooth compatible speaker and mic for personal functions.

Bibliophiles can enjoy a good collection of books available on deck, and the younger guests can play board games provided by the houseboat

Conoce la historia de  “las Aloha”, una historia de amor, arrojo, perseverancia y victorias, en la que eso que muchos consideran desecho les permitió soñar con un final feliz.

title: Seeking South
description:
Seeking South follows trail runner Keisuke Minami as he takes on the fastest-known-time (FKT) challenge of the Grand Randonée 10 (GR10)—a grueling 914 km journey across the Pyrenees in southern France, from the Atlantic to the Mediterranean. The route typically takes 45-60 days to complete, but Minami sets out to finish in just over 9 days.

Why would someone willingly endure pain, isolation, and total exhaustion? What might keep him running? Minami, whose name means "south" in Japanese, runs across the mountains as the film pursues the story behind his relentless drive.

A story of obsession, resilience, and the demons that push us forward, Seeking South is an intimate look at the mind of an endurance athlete and the weight of the past he runs to escape—or embrace.

title: These Activists Track Wolverines and the Impact of Climate Change
description:
To celebrate 40+ years of environmental grantmaking at Patagonia, we’re sharing brand-new stories from our longtime nonprofit partners like the Cascades Wolverine Project, which blends science, storytelling and recreation to support wolverine recovery for the benefit of people and wildlife. 

Rain or shine, the team skis out to remote wolverine habitat sites across the Pacific Northwest to set up cameras, monitors the sites throughout the seasons and then shares the data they collect to advance further research and community science efforts.

“Wolverines depend on deep snow in order to survive,” says Stephanie Williams, the group’s cofounder. “Tracking whether or not they can adapt to this changing climate means that we’re also in some ways tracking our own fate.” 

Learn more about Cascades Wolverine Project at https://pat.ag/YT/Cascades.

description:
To celebrate 40+ years of environmental grantmaking at Patagonia, we’re sharing brand-new stories from our longtime nonprofit partners like the Cascades Wolverine Project, which blends science, storytelling and recreation to support wolverine recovery for the benefit of people and wildlife.

title: Why Southern Forests Are Disappearing 4x Faster Than the Amazon
description:
To celebrate 40+ years of environmental grantmaking at Patagonia, we’re sharing brand-new stories from longtime partners like the Dogwood Alliance, which mobilizes people to protect forests and communities from industrial logging in the Southern US.   

“Trees are the solution for pollution. But when you start cutting those trees up, turning them into pellets and then burning them for energy, it creates a major human problem,” says Treva Gear, the Georgia campaign manager for Dogwood Alliance.  

More than a million acres of US forests have already been cut for biomass, directly exposing frontline communities to heavy pollution. Leaders like Treva are part of a growing movement to stop even more destruction in forests and communities across the South. 
 
“We’re going to fight and push back against this industry to protect our trees, to protect our health, to protect our planet.”  

Learn more about Dogwood Alliance at https://pat.ag/YT/Dogwood.

Tucked deep in southern Chile, Cochamó Valley has long felt untouched - no roads cutting through it, no engines overhead, just rainforest, granite walls and the people who call it home. When the land was put up for sale, the future of this place hung in the balance. What followed wasn’t a takeover by developers or investors, but something far rarer: a community stepping forward to protect what they love.

At its heart are the local residents, climbers, conservationists and neighbors who came together to secure Fundo Puchegüín and ensure its protection far into the future. Their work connects millions of acres of protected land across Chile and Argentina and introduces a new model of conservation - one led by the people who live on the land, shaped by shared responsibility, and grounded in care for future generations.

Cochamó’s story is proof that protecting wild places doesn’t have to mean excluding people. Sometimes it means trusting them.

title: Cochamó por siempre | Una victoria de conservación que nace desde la comunidad
description:
¡Victoria en Chile! La compra exitosa del Fundo Puchegüín, liderada por Conserva Puchegüín, proyecta un nuevo futuro para la conservación y establece un gran logro para nuestro hogar, el planeta Tierra.  

En diciembre pasado, Conserva Puchegüín -una coalición de organizaciones dedicadas a la conservación, científicos y miembros de la comunidad local- concretó la compra de un territorio de alto valor ecológico conocido como el Fundo Puchegüín. Con el apoyo de Holdfast Collective, la organización sin fines de lucro de Patagonia, esta adquisición protege para siempre su biodiversidad, las costumbres y modos de vida de sus habitantes, así como su valor como espacio para las actividades y deportes al aire libre, tanto en el valle de Cochamó como en sus alrededores.  

Lo que sigue ahora es el desarrollo de un nuevo modelo de conservación, liderado y cocreado por personas que aman, defienden y habitan este territorio, que marca un hito para nuestro planeta.

description:
Some people make a living from their craft. Others can’t live without it. In a 16th century mill in the Chamonix valley, Peter and Anati run Le Moulin des Artistes: a ski workshop, art space, and gathering place for like-minded free spirits. Whether it’s in Peter’s handmade wooden skis or Anati’s paintings and music, Le Moulin des Artistes shows us what happens when you devote your life to creative expression. How it can bring purpose, build lasting community, and even help overcome disaster.

In rural Pennsylvania, along the banks of the Allegheny River, snowboard filmmaker Bryden Bowley has quietly built a collection of used Patagonia gear that spans 50 years. Watch the short film to learn how his obsession, snowboarding and a love of the natural world led him to see ownership as an antidote to overconsumption.

title: Offseason: Marie-France Roy | Patagonia
description:
Marie-France Roy’s world is shaped by connection, from snow-covered mountains to the kelp forests of the Pacific Ocean.

A Patagonia Snow ambassador based on the coast of British Columbia, Marie spends her winters riding big mountain lines. But in the offseason, her focus shifts downstream, quite literally, toward the ocean and the ecosystems that depend on it.

Patagonia Snowboard ambassador Marie-France Roy’s world is connected by snow up high and kelp down low. When she’s not riding big mountains, she’s working to help the kelp forests off British Columbia thrive.

Drawn to the wildness of the coast, Marie has developed a deep connection to kelp, a fast-growing marine plant that supports biodiversity, captures carbon and plays a critical role in ocean health. Through drone mapping and collaboration with local conservation groups, she’s helping monitor kelp beds and better understand how they’re changing over time.

For Marie, everything is connected. Snow falling high in the mountains eventually makes its way to the ocean, linking environments that might seem far apart. That perspective shapes how she moves through both, whether on a snowboard or in the water.

Watch our “Offseason” series to learn more about what our ambassadors are up to when the wetsuits, waders and bibs come off.

When he hooks and lands a chrome-bright wild steelhead on a fly he created himself, the moment feels less like conquest than connection. Through quiet observation, “Oly’s Dean” captures a childhood rooted in independence and stewardship—and parents learning to see the world with a renewed sense of wonder.

title: Swiftcurrent Waders | Innovation Built on Exploration
description:
More than five decades of outdoor leadership have taught us a few things about building waders: the value of reliability, the advantages of intuitive design and the importance of accountability to our customers and our planet. We are never finished learning, questioning, tinkering and improving.
 
To bring our 2025 Swiftcurrent Waders to life, we listened to customer feedback, analyzed dozens of new fabrics, auditioned different material combinations and evaluated countless fit, design and feature tweaks. Our team of hardcore field testers punished prototype after prototype for more than three years of on-the-water testing and refinement.
 
Built with innovative materials, intuitive features and a refined fit, our Swiftcurrent® Waders are a better wader experience. Repatterned for bulk reduction, reduced seam stress, increased maneuverability and improved repairability, they move better in and out of the water, carry gear more efficiently and keep tools handy. They adjust to temperature changes better and switch from chest-high to waist-high quickly. They’re made from recycled materials without intentionally added “forever chemicals” known as PFAS. We even pattern them so they’re easier to put on, take off, and repair.
 
Motivated by relentless curiosity and a passion for the wild fish and clean waters we love, Patagonia Fly Fishing is thrilled to present the 2025 Swiftcurrent Wader Line.

title: Meet Austen
description:
Austen “the Froth Goblin” Sweetin is Pacific Northwest, through and through. Born in Seattle, Washington, he’s been shaped by both the area’s deep snowboarding culture and steep, technical terrain since his earliest years, a background that’s made him one of the sport’s most versatile and exciting riders. He can power down Alaskan spines as smoothly as he can 10-story pillow stacks, all while spinning and tricking off every feature like a cat on a bender. Now Austen is taking those freeride skills to the skintrack, using human power to find new lines and chase after bigger objectives. 
 
“The thing that really keeps me getting after it is the ceiling, the unknown,” he says. “What’s the next forecast going to look like? What’s this mountain range going to be like? It’s that constant evolution, that newness, that keeps me pursuing at a deeper level.” 
That passion and energy have made him one of snowboarding’s most beloved figures, and whether you’re watching him surf, skate or pick riffs on his guitar, Austen makes you want to go snowboarding.

title: Meet Lucas
description:
Lucas Wachs is a snowboarder’s skier; he never misses a side hit and rarely goes in a straight line. Having grown up on the natural terrain park of Mt. Bachelor riding with mostly snowboarders, the Bend, Oregon, local was destined to be unconventional: his slashy, surfy style turns any slope into a playground, with a versatility that defies labels or disciplines. Lucas brings that mindset to everything he rides, from PNW pillows to Alaskan spines to touring up one of Oregon’s volcanoes, and he’s more interested than ever to explore where the skintrack can take him. 
 
He’s also a badass mountain biker, skateboarder, snowboarder and surfer, skills that continue to influence his skiing. Whatever Lucas is doing, you can guarantee two things: He’ll do it his own way, and he’ll do it with style. 
 
“As a skier, I think I look at the mountains in different ways,” he says. “I learned a lot from snowboarders growing up and how they approach terrain, and I think that set me apart from other people. Not better; just a different take.”

title: Meet Jack
description:
For a 21-year-old, Jack Ho has had a hell of a career. Born and raised on O‘ahu, Hawai‘i, right next to the world-famous beaches of Waikiki, Jack started surfing when he was 5 years old and he hasn’t left the water since. That passion only intensified when, at age 13, his dad bought him a foil, which he pursued with a dedication that would quickly make him one of the best in the world. Two years later, he and a group of friends discovered downwinders, and the “Voyager Foilers” have spent the past half-decade pushing the limits of what’s possible on a foil … though Jack can still be found off the shore of O‘ahu paddling his short and longboards to catch the next swell. 

“My love for surfing started at a young age, and no matter what I do, I can’t shake it off,” he says. “It’s a passion that sticks with me, and the root of it is riding waves every type of way, getting out there and enjoying what my home has to offer. That’s so valuable to me and something I take a lot of pride in.” 

So hyped to get on the water with you, Jack. Welcome to the team.

title: Meet Jenny
description:
Jenny’s path to mountain exploration started in the North Cascades, backpacking with her family. She caught the rock-climbing bug in her mid-20s, lived in a van and traveled with the conditions, ticking off well-respected alpine routes in Canada, Patagonia and Europe. During COVID, Jenny discovered a penchant for running and took it into the mountains, rediscovering areas she’d often been with a heavy climbing kit. She loved how much faster she could go with just a lightweight pack. Jenny started expanding the traditional definition of trail running, mixing technical rock skills with the simplicity of running. Her favorite form of mountain expression involves long, complex routes that mix trail and off-trail travel, just seeing how far and she can get.   

“It doesn’t matter whether you call it trail running, or mountain running or ultra-neering,” she says. “Moving through the mountains unencumbered by a heavy load is a special form of freedom.”  

Excited to do some exploring with you, Jenny. Welcome to the team.

title: Meet Cash
description:
Cash is what happens when you give a surfboard wings. Born and raised on Maui, the young waterman has been surfing his entire life and picked up foiling in his mid-teens. Cash surfs when the waves are clean and the wind is down; when they’re not, his foil turns bumps and chop into a magic carpet ride, allowing him to stay out on the water longer with his friends, be it in the ocean or on a lake or river. As he puts it, “a one-foot wave on a foil can feel like a six-foot wave on a surfboard.” 
 
Despite just turning 20 years old, Cash is already pushing the boundaries of what’s possible on a foil with a unique style that’s as playful as it is cutting edge, so much so that he has a signature technique, the Berzolla Bottom Turn. Whatever he’s riding, Cash is just happy to be on the water. 

“Being on land can be so crazy and can make life feel super intense,” he says. “But when I hop in the water, I’m focused on one thing and one thing only. It brings me a peace of mind, helps me relax and most importantly, it’s fun.” 

Hyped to catch some waves with you, Cash. Welcome to the team.

title: I Skied Down Mount Everest (world first, no oxygen)
description:
Ski mountaineer Andrzej Bargiel becomes the first person to climb Mount Everest and ski back to Everest Base Camp without supplementary oxygen. After nearly 16 hours climbing in the high altitude “death zone” (above 8,000m where oxygen levels are dangerously low), Bargiel clipped into his skis on the summit of the tallest mountain on earth and started his descent via the South Col Route. He reached Camp II that night and rested - the summit ridge and Hillary Step had taken longer than planned, meaning darkness made it dangerous and difficult to navigate further that day. The next morning, he skied through the treacherous Khumbu Icefall - guided by a drone flown by his brother, Bartek - before safely arriving at Base Camp to become the first person to ascend and descend Mount Everest on skis with no supplementary oxygen.

description:

Discover how to elevate your listening experience by enabling 'Ultra high quality (UHQ) audio', using adaptive Equalizer, and experiencing clearer calls with Super Clear Call. 00:00 Intro

Follow these steps to get the most out of your Hi-Fi sound on Galaxy Buds4 Pro:
Wearing the earbuds
Step 1: Insert the earbuds comfortably in your ears.
Step 2: Once the fit is detected, you’ll hear a brief sound feedback.
Step 3: Run a fit test in your Galaxy Buds settings to check your fit.
Step 4: Adjust if needed until you get a ‘Good fit’.
Advanced sound settings 
Step 1: Go to your Galaxy Buds settings.
Step 2: In 'Sound quality and effects', you can set features like '360 audio', and the Equalizer.
Step 3: In 'Advanced quality options', you can enable 'Ultra high quality (UHQ) audio' and 'Super wide band speech'.

Q: What is Advanced 2-way speaker?
A: Galaxy Buds4 Pro features the Advanced 2-way speaker system. The system includes a wider woofer and a tweeter, each handling tailored frequency ranges to reproduce sound as originally intended with minimum distortion. The new wider woofer with a 19.8 % larger diaphragm than Galaxy Buds3 Pro, delivers natural, high-quality bass, while precise tuning maintains phase coherence for unified Hi-Fi sound. And independent dual amplifiers ensure clarity, rich mids, and solid bass. 
Q: What is the Samsung Seamless Codec (SSC) ‘Ultra high quality (UHQ) audio’ option?
A: The ‘Ultra high quality (UHQ) audio' option supports 24-bit / 96 kHz audio with eligible Samsung Galaxy devices. It preserves the original sound with vast amount of information while maintaining stable connections.
Q: What is Super Clear Call?
A: Super Clear Call enhances voice clarity during calls, even in noisy environments. A machine-learned Deep Neural Network (DNN) reduces background noise and focuses on your voice.

title: What is an NFT? Explained in 59 seconds #shorts
description:
You’ve probably heard about this thing called an “NFT” but what is it, and why do you need to know about it?
In short, NFT stands for non-fungible token. 
If an asset is fungible it means it can be replaced or exchanged and its value will stay the same. For example, 5 $20 bills have the same value as 1 $100 bill. 
Therefore, non-fungible assets cannot be substituted. These are assets like land, homes, or even baseball cards. Their value is defined by their own unique qualities which can take away, or add value. 
Now those examples are physical.  NFTs are digital assets, or, tokens.
